strings.name: Timnit Gebru
strings.role: AI researcher · DAIR founder and executive director
strings.summary: Timnit Gebru studies AI bias, datasets and technology’s social effects. She founded and leads DAIR, advocating independent, community-rooted research. She previously co-led Google’s Ethical AI team and co-founded Black in AI with Rediet Abebe. Her papers and initiatives involve many collaborators and examine who shapes technology and bears its effects.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Historical model studies and current systems, draft and published papers, and award announcements and ceremonies are distinguished. Both accounts of her Google departure are retained.
strings.influence.rationale: Researches AI bias, datasets and social impacts, advancing independent research and public discussion of algorithmic accountability.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Stanford bachelor’s, master’s and doctorate in electrical engineering; completed her PhD in 2017 under Fei-Fei Li.
strings.facts.f2.label: Research experience
strings.facts.f2.value: Postdoctoral work in Microsoft Research New York’s FATE group on algorithmic bias and ethical questions in data research.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Intersectional auditing
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Joy Buolamwini, studied group error disparities in historical commercial gender classifiers, not all face-recognition systems.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Improving dataset documentation
strings.highlights.h2.text: With collaborators, proposed documenting data provenance, composition and recommended uses.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joins AFROTECH discussion
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discusses AI’s human costs and data accountability in Houston, urging attention to affected communities; subsequent reporting confirms the speaking date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Right Livelihood Award announced
strings.timeline.t2.text: The organizer recognizes her AI-accountability research; the December 1 ceremony remains future, not an attended event.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Founds DAIR
strings.timeline.t3.text: Launches an independent, interdisciplinary institute for community-rooted AI research.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Co-authors Stochastic Parrots paper
strings.timeline.t4.text: With Emily M. Bender, Angelina McMillan-Major and the author credited as Shmargaret Shmitchell, discusses large language models’ costs and data risks.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Leaves Google’s Ethical AI team
strings.timeline.t5.text: She says she was fired; Google says it accepted her resignation. The dispute involved paper review and workplace conditions; their accounts differ.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Datasheets for Datasets preprint released
strings.timeline.t6.text: With six co-authors, proposes dataset documentation; the journal version appears in 2021.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-publishes Gender Shades
strings.timeline.t7.text: With Joy Buolamwini, evaluates three commercial gender classifiers, finding error disparities across skin-tone and gender groups.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Co-founds Black in AI
strings.timeline.t8.text: Establishes the membership organization with Rediet Abebe to support Black AI practitioners; nonprofit status is finalized in 2018.
